# Complete test inventory

This is a source-derived inventory of every discovered test method, audited on 2026-10-15. Functionality descriptions use method docstrings or scenario names, with assertion and call evidence in [the JSON inventory](test_inventory.json). These are intended coverage claims, **not measured statement or branch coverage**.

Markdown shows at most the first two assertion expressions, shortened to 260 characters. JSON retains every direct assertion expression, lexical production-call candidates, interface calls, helper references and their shared assertion evidence, loops, subtest sites, decorators and fixture calls. Dynamic dispatch and inherited fixture behavior require source inspection; this is not a manually proven call graph or an exhaustive enumeration of runtime subtest cases.

Total: **2,823 methods in 248 test files**. A method can contain many subtests, input cases or expensive executions. Those are not separate unittest methods.

Discovery reconciliation: exact match, 2,823 canonical unittest IDs; zero discovery errors.

Historical status and method seconds come from `artifacts/test-suite-speed-completed-segments-v1.json`. Class setup/teardown, discovery and interpreter shutdown are not allocated to methods. A dash means no method duration was recorded, not zero cost. Runtime skips can differ by environment; their exact historical reasons are in JSON.

Regenerate: `.venv\Scripts\python.exe tools/audit_test_inventory.py --collect`. This imports modules for discovery but never runs tests or setup fixtures. Without the ignored historical receipts, use `--without-history`; historical status/timing fields are then unrecorded.

See [the multi-pass audit](../TEST_INFRASTRUCTURE_AUDIT.md) for overlap, cost and infrastructure findings.
